summary: Bounded audit of s03 network option parsers that read a size byte and use it unclamped. All TCP-option walkers checked (tcp_input.c tcp_parse_options/tcp_parse_mss_option, mptcp_get_options, nf_conntrack_proto_tcp tcp_options/tcp_sack, nf_synproxy_core synproxy_parse_options, core/filter.c bpf_search_tcp_opt) contain the length<2 plus opsize<=length guards. One credible candidate found: net/netfilter/xt_dccp.c dccp_find_option walks DCCP options reading op[i+1] as a size byte without any (optlen - i) >= 2 guard and without clamping op[i+1] to remaining bytes, unlike the sibling xt_tcpmss.c which guards 'i == optlen - 1'.

candidates.reason: i += op[i+1]?:1 reads a size byte with no 2-byte-remaining check and no clamp to optlen
tcp_parse_options has length<2 return plus opsize>length return before any body use
tcp_parse_fastopen_option clamps len to [TCP_FASTOPEN_COOKIE_MIN, TCP_FASTOPEN_COOKIE_MAX] before memcpy; callers pass opsize-derived len with opsize<=length already enforced
mptcp_get_options in this tree already contains the length<2 fix (seed patch applied)
tcp_options/tcp_sack have length<2 and opsize>length guards before body reads
bpf_search_tcp_opt checks opend-op<2, opend-op<op[1], op[1]>=2 before use
guard 'op[i] < 2 || i == optlen - 1' prevents final-byte size read; MSS read also has (optlen-i)>=TCPOLEN_MSS
optlen() reads opt[offset+1] but caller loop bound i < tcp_hdrlen - 1 ensures offset+1 within header
